{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
In [[algebraic topology]], a branch of mathematics, an '''approximate fibration''' is a sort of [[fibration]] such that the [[homotopy lifting property]] holds only approximately. The notion was introduced by Coram and Duvall in 1977.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=D. |last1=Coram |first2=P. |last2=Duvall |title=Approximate fibrations |journal=Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics |volume=7 |date=1977 |issue=2 |pages=275–288 |doi=10.1216/RMJ-1977-7-2-275|doi-access=free }}</ref>

A '''manifold approximate fibration''' is a proper approximate fibration between manifolds.<ref>{{harvnb|Hughes|Taylor|Williams|1995|loc=§ 1.}}</ref> Some authors believe that manifold approximate fibrations are the "correct bundle theory for topological manifolds and singular spaces".<ref>{{harvnb|Hughes|Taylor|Williams|1995|loc=Introduction}}</ref>
